pack.risks: unvalidated idea; tiny DEMO risk only

concerns: affected_files cites bot/intel/ and bot/ai_council/, but the actual modification target is bot/aegis/research/promote.py; the manifest does not match the change
expected_mechanism 'improve exploration/validation throughput' contradicts the effect: a stricter CI-bound gate reduces promotion throughput; it improves selectivity/precision, not volume

rescoring every previously logged challenger against the same sealed holdout creates multiplicity/data-snooping pressure; nominal 95% coverage degrades under repeated reuse unless explicitly controlled
no minimum effective trade count or power statement: with sparse holdout trades the CI lower bound will rarely clear zero, risking silent champion starvation
block length, bootstrap replicate count, and RNG seed policy are unspecified, so the gate is not reproducible as written
undefined whether the CI condition is conjunctive with existing promote.py gates, and whether retrospective rescoring can demote already-recorded challengers or applies prospectively only
tests field is vague: no named unit tests for the bootstrap scorer, no edge cases (zero trades, degenerate return series), no suite-green commitment
votes.reason: Directionally sound and safety-aligned: replacing a positive point estimate of net OOS expectancy with a 95% block-bootstrap CI lower bound strictly above zero, on the sealed holdout, net of runner spread/slippage, with blocks respecting each candidate's own horizon, only tightens champion promotion. It touches no execution path, no protected trading YAML, and requires no MT5 mutation, and it is falsifiable from existing records. However, the proposal contains internal inconsistencies (wrong affected_files, contradictory mechanism claim) and unresolved statistical-design gaps (holdout reuse multiplicity, unspecified block length/replicates/sample floor) that must be fixed before implementation.

votes.reason: The proposed shift from a point-estimate gate (PF > 1) to a 95% block-bootstrap confidence interval lower bound (p05 > 0) on sealed holdout data is a standard robustness improvement in systematic trading. It significantly reduces the probability of Type I errors (false discoveries) during the promotion phase by ensuring that expectancy is statistically significant net of dependencies and costs. The use of block-bootstrap, specifically accounting for trade horizon overlap, is appropriate for time-series data where returns may exhibit autocorrelation. This change enhances the rigor of the promotion process without introducing live risk.
